memo.headline: Prioritize billing/support, starting with free-tier restrictions
memo.recommendation: Baseline issue ranking is: 1) billing.free_tier_limits, priority_score 153530 [C1]; 2) other.general, 136310 [C2]; 3) usability.ads, 85196 [C3]; 4) playback.stops_skips, 55806 [C4]. Do not treat other.general as a product fix: it is non-specific feedback, with 68092 complaints [C5]. Start with billing.free_tier_limits: billing_support’s complaint share rose from 4.6% in the baseline to 21.9% in the most recent complete months, the largest current share and increase among the focus areas. This spike is review evidence, not proof of cause. The issue is also the top baseline issue; customer quotes mention restrictions on skips and lyrics. The recent volume and growth make it the best next-quarter focus, while the high baseline score reinforces that choice.

alternatives.why_lower: Usability remains a substantial alternative: its complaint share increased from 11.8% to 18.5%, and usability.ads ranks third in the baseline at 85196 [C3]. But billing_support’s recent share is higher, and usability’s increase is smaller. Address ads and UI complaints after the billing/support spike.

Playback’s complaint share fell from 8.1% to 5.0%. playback.stops_skips ranks fourth at 55806 [C4], and the playback area has 10976 severity-4-or-5 records, so reliability issues remain serious. The higher-ranked free-tier and ad issues call for billing/support and usability work; playback should follow unless service monitoring indicates an urgent reliability problem.

Access has the highest area mean severity (3.852582) and 7923 severity-4-or-5 records, but its recent complaint share is 1.9%, below its 1.2% baseline only in relative terms? Its share rose from 1.2% to 1.9%, but current volume remains lower than billing_support and usability. access.login_failure is a serious targeted issue, not the strongest overall next-quarter focus.

limitations: These are self-selected historical Google Play reviews from 2022-05-17 to 2023-11-15, not a representative measure of all users.
The classification queue began with a uniform seeded 100,000-review sample and expanded to distinct nonempty texts; 20 nonempty rows were unclassified, and 13 empty texts were quarantined.
Model labels can be wrong; identical texts reuse saved results.
Cancellation language is expressed intent, not observed churn.
